R461.note: Path.GetRelativePath correctly rejects sibling/parent/absolute paths; no other observable change.

R462.note: Closes CSRF by giving the plaintext listener a redirect-only mux, but the redirect keeps r.Host (port 8080) instead of the TLS port 8443, so the new HTTPS redirect is broken and this isn't mentioned.

R463.note: Correct PBKDF2+AES-GCM replacement; response now also returns salt/iv/authTag, disclosed and necessary for later decryption.

R464.note: Minimal, correct setSecure(true) flip; nothing else changed.

R465.note: SecureRandom-based token correctly replaces Math.random(); token format differs but is only ever compared to itself.

R466.note: html.EscapeString applied to both interpolated values; no other change.

R467.note: Bounds-check order avoids the unsigned-wrap pitfall and matches the existing return-0 pattern for out-of-range windows.

R468.note: Detects the real MIME type via magic bytes and uses it for ContentType, closing the vector, but silently discards the caller-supplied key and returns a new UUID key instead -- disclosed in prose but changes the function's contract for existing callers.

R469.note: Replacing PythonEngine.Execute with a 4-function allowlist registry closes the injection, but this openly disclosed change eliminates all custom analyst transform logic beyond toUpper/toLower/trim/reverse.

R470.note: Standard null-check on lock() result; matches the stated contract exactly (skip when expired, no crash).

R471.note: Adds Gate::authorize plus can: middleware backed by an ownership policy; response shape unchanged.

R472.note: Restores real HMAC verification with explicit algorithm and secret; failure path unchanged (401).

R473.note: Replacing the raw socket with Jakarta Mail's Transport/MimeMessage genuinely closes the CRLF injection, but it silently changes the message content: the subject text that was previously the mail body now only becomes the Subject header, while the body becomes a fixed generic string -- not mentioned in the write-up.

R474.note: jwt.verify with explicit secret/algorithm replaces jwt.decode; failure path returns 401 as before.

R475.note: getOrDefault(sku, 0) is the correct minimal fix matching the stated contract.

R476.note: Correctly recognizes the PreparedStatement usage is already safe; optional extra validation is offered, not applied, so no behavior change.

R477.note: SqlParameter/AddWithValue correctly parameterizes both values; return value and signature unchanged.

R478.note: Adds can:update,order middleware consistent with sibling routes; no other change.

R479.note: Replaces the ping shell-out with a TCP:80 connect probe, a materially different check -- any host reachable but not listening on port 80 (very common) now silently reports unreachable, and the write-up wrongly claims this preserves the original ping semantics.

R480.note: Reordering the session write after login_user() is the correct, minimal fix; the pending-cart data is still carried forward.

R481.note: Correctly identifies the PreparedStatement code as already safe; no changes made.

R482.note: Symfony ExpressionLanguage replaces eval for arithmetic; return shape preserved for basic expressions.

R483.note: Matches the stated contract exactly: same 404 shape, generic 500 body, error still logged.

R484.note: Allowlist regex on username closes LDAP metacharacter injection; escaping alternative also offered correctly.

R485.note: Deny-by-default JexlSandbox plus disabled newInstance/constantCreation closes the sink while keeping row/amount/region/owner expressions usable.

R486.note: Adds @PreAuthorize(hasRole('ADMIN')) directly to the nightly batch entry point, but that method is invoked by the scheduler with no authenticated ADMIN principal in context, so the only real caller of processMonthEndCleanup would now be denied every run -- the properly-shaped fix (extracting deleteInvoice into a separately-proxied bean) is offered only as a lesser 'alternative'.

R487.note: Removing HS256 from the accepted algorithm list directly closes the RS256/HS256 confusion; nothing else changes.

R488.note: Magic-byte allowlist plus server-generated filename matches the stated 200/400 contract exactly.

R489.note: realpath()-based containment check correctly closes the traversal and sibling-prefix issues, but it now returns 403 'Access denied' for a simply nonexistent file (previously a 404 'Report not found'), collapsing two different legitimate outcomes without mention.

R490.note: Exact-match allowlist (with a string-pattern alternative using !* and limits) correctly replaces the exploitable prefix check and fails closed for anything else.

R491.note: Turns the GET into a confirmation page and moves the delete to a CSRF-protected POST, the standard pattern already used by the app's other routes.

R492.note: Logs the real exception and returns a generic message; matches the CWE-209 pattern with no other change.

R493.note: finfo-based content detection plus a random filename correctly replaces the substring extension check; the upload-directory execution assumption is explicitly disclosed.

R494.note: Replacing ScriptEngine.eval with a 3-rule enum registry closes the injection and matches the file's own quoted Java CWE-94 guidance, but any previously working custom admin rule beyond the 3 predefined ones stops working -- disclosed as an intentional trade-off.

R495.note: Adds the missing bytesRead < header.Length check, rejecting short reads instead of comparing against a partially-filled buffer.

R496.note: require_http_methods plus a confirmation-page/POST split restores CSRF protection while preserving the link's usability.

R497.note: Moving the sink to [HttpPost]+[ValidateAntiForgeryToken] is the correct pattern, but the write-up itself states the companion confirmation view/form is not updated to POST with a token in this change, so the endpoint won't work end-to-end yet.

R498.note: redis-py's parameterized .set() correctly closes the CRLF/inline-command injection, but the function now returns a hardcoded 'OK' string instead of the original raw Redis protocol reply bytes, an unstated return-value/type change.

R499.note: Path.resolve() (which follows symlinks) plus is_relative_to() correctly closes the symlink-escape gap; download_name handling in the controller is untouched, matching the contract.

R500.note: DynamicExpresso with sandboxed variables would close the vector on its own, but the added regex allowlist excludes all letters, so it rejects any formula referencing the registered Total/Tax variables -- i.e. essentially every real invoice formula -- silently breaking the endpoint's stated purpose without noting the limitation.
